hypothesis: The neuron responds selectively to high-contrast, dark focal objects—typically black, charcoal, dark brown, or deep maroon—set against a lighter, often uniform background. The activating features consistently present as compact, rounded, or elongated forms, encompassing diverse semantic categories such as birds, dogs, dried flowers, stove burners, circular displays, and dark pillows. The neuron remains invariant to the object's specific identity, surface texture, or material, as long as the strong tonal polarity between the dark subject and the lighter surroundings is preserved. The background usually consists of pale, desaturated, or cool tones, specifically white, off-white, beige, light grey, or sky blue. The activating feature typically occupies approximately 15–40% of the image area and is generally positioned near the center or along the horizontal midline of the frame.
